purpose: machine-readable ontology for the conceptual feedback-loop layer of system dynamics as evaluable modeling/diagnosis work-units: framing a system boundary and reference mode, identifying stocks/flows/delays, tracing loops and signing links, classifying loop polarity (reinforcing/balancing), finding the dominant loop and dominance shifts, building causal-loop and stock-and-flow diagrams, matching system archetypes, and locating leverage, tipping points, exponential growth, overshoot-and-collapse, and unintended consequences; a subdomain node of systems thinking, feedback loops and control for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB (the math/stability layer lives in a sibling subdomain).
assumptions: Feedback Loops & System Dynamics is modeled as a subdomain of systems thinking, feedback loops and control.
Nodes are concrete, evaluable loop modeling and diagnosis work-units (identify a loop, classify polarity, find the dominant loop, locate leverage), not generic 'systems' topics.
This is the conceptual loop layer; the quantitative stability/control-math layer (eigenvalues, transfer functions, bifurcation math) lives in a sibling subdomain and is excluded.
No observed dataset or experimental evidence is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Scope follows Meadows 'Thinking in Systems', Sterman 'Business Dynamics', and Weinberg 'An Introduction to General Systems Thinking'.
exclusions: Quantitative stability analysis, eigenvalue/transfer-function/bifurcation math, and numerical-integration parameterization (sibling subdomain).
Statistical estimation, calibration, and data fitting of model parameters.
Domain-specific simulation tooling and software engineering of simulation models.
Control-engineering controller design and signal-processing methods beyond the conceptual feedback layer.

competency_questions.question: Given a symptom and a decision, what is the model purpose, reference mode, and endogenous/exogenous boundary?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SYSTEM_BOUNDARY_PURPOSE yields purpose, reference mode, boundary

competency_questions.question: For each in-scope variable, is it a stock or a flow, and what are its inflows and outflows?
What feedback loops exist, what is each link's sign, and is each loop reinforcing or balancing?
How does a loop's polarity predict the qualitative behavior (growth, decline, goal-seeking) it produces?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOOP_POLARITY and EXPONENTIAL_GROWTH map polarity to behavior

competency_questions.question: Which loop currently dominates behavior, and where should leverage be applied?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOOP_DOMINANCE and LEVERAGE_POINT answer dominance and leverage

competency_questions.question: When and why does loop dominance shift over time?
Where do delays cause oscillation, overshoot, fixes-that-fail, or policy resistance?
Where are the nonlinearities, tipping points, and overshoot-and-collapse risks?
How is the feedback structure rendered as a causal-loop and a stock-and-flow diagram?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLD_CONSTRUCTION and SFD_CONSTRUCTION produce the diagrams

competency_questions.question: For a candidate intervention, what are its likely unintended consequences and policy-resistance risks?
Does the proposed structure reproduce the reference mode and known behavior patterns?
How are nonlinear thresholds bounded when no precise data is available?
What triggers a revisit of the dominance hypothesis or the loop structure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BEHAVIOR_VALIDATION feedback edges and revisit triggers

competency_questions.question: How are stakeholder mental models elicited and reconciled into the loop structure?

glossary.definition: a feedback loop with an even number of negative links that amplifies change (growth or collapse)
a feedback loop with an odd number of negative links that seeks a goal and resists change
an accumulation that changes only through its flows and gives a system memory and inertia
a rate that fills or drains a stock per unit time
the property that one loop's strength controls behavior in a given phase
a place in the structure where a small change yields a large lasting behavior change
a lag between a cause and its effect; material delays move quantities, information delays move perception
the behavior-over-time pattern the model must explain or reproduce
a threshold where a small change pushes the system into a different, often irreversible regime
a recurring loop structure that produces a characteristic problematic behavior

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established system-dynamics and systems-thinking literature (Meadows 2008; Sterman 2000; Weinberg 1975; Senge 1990) and modeling practice; no measured dataset supplied.
does_not_support: observed loop strengths or delay durations
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Set the model purpose, dynamic problem (reference mode over time), time horizon, and the boundary separating endogenous variables from exogenous drivers.
contradictors: modeler who maps every variable with no purpose

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the reference problem or time horizon is restated, changing what is endogenous

pros.claim: a stated purpose and boundary make the model falsifiable and bounded
pros.example: purpose: explain why sales overshot then collapsed over 5 years

pros.claim: endogenizing the right drivers prevents blaming external scapegoats
pros.example: treating capacity as endogenous, not 'bad luck'

cons.claim: too narrow a boundary hides the loop that actually drives behavior
cons.example: excluding word-of-mouth from an adoption model

cons.claim: too wide a boundary makes the model unbounded and unsolvable
cons.example: modeling the whole economy to study one product

failure_modes: laundry-list of variables with no dynamic problem
boundary drawn to exclude the dominant loop
static snapshot instead of behavior over time
acceptance_tests: a reference mode graph (variable vs time) is drawn
each key variable labeled endogenous or exogenous with reason
purpose names the behavior to be explained
revisit_triggers: an excluded variable turns out to drive the dynamics

nodes.definition: Identify stocks (accumulations), the flows (rates) that fill or drain them, and distinguish a level from its rate of change for each in-scope variable.
contradictors: analyst who treats every variable as an instantaneous rate
outputs: inflow and outflow list per stock

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a quantity reclassified between stock and flow changes the accumulation structure

pros.claim: separating stocks from flows reveals where accumulation and inertia live
pros.example: inventory is a stock; shipments are a flow

pros.claim: the bathtub test (stock changes only via flows) catches structural errors early
pros.example: population changes only via births/deaths/migration

cons.claim: misclassifying a stock as a flow corrupts every downstream loop
cons.example: treating 'morale' as a flow not an accumulation

cons.claim: some soft variables resist clean stock/flow typing
cons.example: reputation as a stock with fuzzy flows

failure_modes: stock and flow conflated
rate confused with level
units inconsistent across a flow and its stock
acceptance_tests: each stock has at least one named inflow or outflow
units of a flow equal units of its stock per time
level-vs-rate labeled for every variable

nodes.definition: Locate material and information delays on flows and links, estimate their duration, and mark them as the structural source of oscillation and overshoot.
contradictors: modeler who assumes instantaneous response

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a delay's length or type (material vs information) is revised

pros.claim: delays are the usual cause of oscillation, overshoot, and instability
pros.example: ordering delay causing bullwhip in a supply chain

pros.claim: naming a perception delay explains why actors react late
pros.example: managers seeing demand only after a reporting lag

cons.claim: ignored delays make a model predict smooth response where reality oscillates
cons.example: assuming hiring is instant in a workforce model

cons.claim: delay duration is hard to estimate without data
cons.example: guessing the perception lag for a new market

failure_modes: delay omitted so oscillation is invisible
material delay confused with information delay
delay duration grossly mis-estimated
acceptance_tests: every flow checked for an upstream delay
each delay tagged material or information
balancing loops containing a delay flagged oscillation-prone
revisit_triggers: oscillation observed that the model lacks

nodes.definition: Trace a closed chain of causal links back to its origin to confirm a feedback loop exists, naming each link's direction and the variable it returns to.
contradictors: analyst who lists one-way causal chains only

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new closed causal chain is found or a link is shown spurious

pros.claim: finding the loop reframes a symptom as endogenous structure, not external shock
pros.example: sales decline traced to a self-reinforcing reputation loop

pros.claim: loop enumeration is the unit every later analysis builds on
pros.example: listing all loops before classifying any

cons.claim: a missed loop means the real driver is invisible
cons.example: omitting the capacity-erosion loop

cons.claim: spurious links create phantom loops
cons.example: drawing a causal link from correlation

failure_modes: open chain mistaken for a closed loop
spurious link closes a phantom loop
loop traced through an exogenous variable
acceptance_tests: each claimed loop returns to its starting variable
every link has a stated causal direction
no loop passes through a purely exogenous node
revisit_triggers: a new link is added or removed
a loop routes through an exogenous driver
reference mode unexplained by current loops

nodes.definition: Assign + or - polarity to each individual causal link based on whether, all else equal, an increase in the cause raises (+) or lowers (-) the effect.
contradictors: modeler who signs links by desirability not direction

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the assumed monotonic relationship on a link is questioned

pros.claim: correct link signs are the atomic input to every loop polarity
pros.example: price up -> quantity demanded down is a negative link

pros.claim: the all-else-equal test makes each sign auditable
pros.example: holding income fixed when signing price->demand

cons.claim: non-monotonic relations resist a single sign
cons.example: stress->performance rising then falling

cons.claim: sign-by-desirability is a common error
cons.example: signing 'pollution->health' positive because more data feels good

failure_modes: sign chosen by whether outcome is desired
non-monotonic link forced to one sign
sign omits the ceteris-paribus condition
acceptance_tests: each link states the all-else-equal direction
non-monotonic links are split or flagged
no sign justified by desirability

nodes.definition: Classify each loop as reinforcing (positive) or balancing (negative) by counting negative links: an even count is reinforcing, an odd count is balancing.
contradictors: analyst who labels loops good/bad instead of by polarity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a single link sign flips, which can invert the whole loop polarity

pros.claim: polarity predicts qualitative behavior: reinforcing grows/collapses, balancing seeks a goal
pros.example: a reinforcing loop drives exponential adoption

pros.claim: parity rule (count negatives) makes classification checkable
pros.example: two negative links => reinforcing

cons.claim: one mis-signed link flips the whole loop's polarity
cons.example: wrongly signing a price-demand link positive

cons.claim: polarity alone does not say which loop wins
cons.example: labeling both loops without ranking them

failure_modes: link sign assigned by intuition not mechanism
parity miscounted
goal-seeking loop mislabeled reinforcing
acceptance_tests: polarity equals parity of negative links
R-loops tied to growth/decline and B-loops to goal-seeking in the narrative
each label cites the counted signs
revisit_triggers: a loop is split or merged

nodes.definition: Determine which feedback loop currently dominates behavior by matching the observed behavior-over-time pattern to the loop whose polarity and strength produce it.
contradictors: analyst who treats all loops as equally active

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: behavior-over-time shifts in a way the current dominant loop cannot produce

pros.claim: only the dominant loop explains current behavior; ranking it focuses intervention
pros.example: exponential phase explained by the reinforcing loop

pros.claim: dominance framing prevents acting on a loop that is currently inactive
pros.example: not fixing a balancing loop that is not yet binding

cons.claim: dominance can be subtle and contested without simulation
cons.example: two plausible loops both fit the early data

cons.claim: static CLDs cannot prove dominance by themselves
cons.example: claiming dominance from a diagram alone

failure_modes: dominance asserted without behavior evidence
equilibrium mistaken for a dead loop
strength inferred from arrow count
acceptance_tests: the dominant loop reproduces the observed behavior pattern
ranking cites behavior, not arrow count
each behavior phase has an assigned dominant loop

nodes.definition: Detect when and why loop dominance shifts over time (e.g., a reinforcing loop yielding to a balancing loop as a limit binds) and locate the transition in the behavior trace.
contradictors: analyst who assumes one loop dominates forever

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a transition point in behavior is observed that the current shift hypothesis misses

pros.claim: most real behavior comes from shifting dominance, not a single loop
pros.example: S-curve = reinforcing then balancing dominance

pros.claim: naming the trigger of a shift tells you which constraint to watch
pros.example: capacity limit triggering the balancing loop

cons.claim: shift timing is hard to pin down without simulation or data
cons.example: guessing when the limit binds

cons.claim: nonlinearity makes shifts abrupt and easy to miss
cons.example: a tipping point crossed before it is noticed

failure_modes: shift ignored, so model predicts unending growth
trigger mis-attributed
inflection placed at the wrong time
acceptance_tests: each behavior inflection has a named dominance shift
each shift cites the loop gaining and the loop losing dominance
the trigger condition for the shift is stated
revisit_triggers: a limit is added or removed

nodes.definition: Assemble signed links and loops into a causal-loop diagram (CLD) with loop-polarity labels, delay marks, and a legend tying the diagram to the reference mode.
contradictors: modeler who draws spaghetti diagrams without loop labels

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a loop or link is added/removed, changing the diagram's loop set

pros.claim: a CLD communicates feedback structure to non-modelers fast
pros.example: one diagram shows the two loops driving overshoot

pros.claim: labeled loops make the diagram auditable, not decorative
pros.example: every loop tagged R or B with a delay mark

cons.claim: CLDs hide stock/flow distinctions and can mislead on accumulation
cons.example: a CLD that looks balanced but accumulates

cons.claim: unlabeled spaghetti diagrams obscure rather than explain
cons.example: 20 arrows, no loop labels

failure_modes: loops drawn but not polarity-labeled
stock/flow nature lost in a pure CLD
delays omitted from the diagram
acceptance_tests: every loop on the diagram carries an R/B label
delays are marked on the relevant links
the diagram maps to the stated reference mode

nodes.definition: Translate the loop structure into a stock-and-flow diagram with stocks, valve-controlled flows, auxiliaries, and information links, preserving units and conservation.
contradictors: modeler who skips stocks and simulates CLDs directly

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a stock, flow, or auxiliary is added/removed, changing accumulation structure

pros.claim: SFDs expose accumulation that CLDs cannot show
pros.example: inventory stock makes the delay's effect explicit

pros.claim: valve-and-stock form is the bridge to simulation
pros.example: structure ready for an integration engine

cons.claim: SFDs are harder for stakeholders to read than CLDs
cons.example: executives lose the thread at the valve symbols

cons.claim: a wrong stock/flow assignment propagates structurally
cons.example: an outflow attached to the wrong stock

failure_modes: flow attached to the wrong stock
conservation violated across a flow
information link drawn as a flow
acceptance_tests: every flow connects to a stock and conserves units
information links carry no material
the SFD reproduces the CLD's loops

nodes.definition: Match a growth-then-stall pattern to the limits-to-growth archetype: a reinforcing engine that runs into a balancing constraint, shifting dominance as the limit binds.

included: pattern matching to the named archetype

contradictors: analyst who treats each problem as unique with no recurring structure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new behavior-over-time data contradicts the current loop hypothesis

pros.claim: identifies the binding constraint as the true leverage, not the growth engine
pros.example: slowing growth fixed by raising the limit, not pushing harder

pros.claim: explains why pushing the reinforcing loop harder stops working
pros.example: more sales effort with no capacity yields nothing

cons.claim: the constraint can be hard to locate before it binds
cons.example: the limit only reveals itself near saturation

cons.claim: can be confused with shifting-the-burden
cons.example: a quick fix masquerading as a limit

failure_modes: pushing growth instead of relaxing the limit
limit identified too late
constraint mistaken for an external shock
acceptance_tests: a reinforcing growth loop and a binding balancing loop are both identified
the slowdown coincides with the limit binding
leverage points at the constraint, not the engine

nodes.definition: Match reliance on a symptomatic quick fix that erodes the fundamental solution to the shifting-the-burden archetype, including the addiction side-effect loop.

included: pattern matching to the named archetype

contradictors: analyst who treats each problem as unique with no recurring structure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new behavior-over-time data contradicts the current loop hypothesis

pros.claim: reveals why a working quick fix makes the problem chronically worse
pros.example: painkillers reducing the push for a cure

pros.claim: locates leverage in strengthening the fundamental solution
pros.example: invest in root-cause capability, not more quick fixes

cons.claim: the eroding side-effect loop is easy to miss
cons.example: not seeing skill atrophy from outsourcing

cons.claim: often mistaken for simple limits-to-growth
cons.example: mislabeling addiction as a constraint

failure_modes: treating the quick fix as the solution
missing the addiction/erosion loop
fundamental solution defunded
acceptance_tests: both a symptomatic and a fundamental solution loop are identified
an erosion or addiction side-effect loop is present
leverage targets the fundamental solution

nodes.definition: Match individually rational use of a shared finite resource that collectively degrades it to the tragedy-of-the-commons archetype, with per-actor reinforcing loops feeding a shared balancing limit.

included: pattern matching to the named archetype

contradictors: analyst who treats each problem as unique with no recurring structure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new behavior-over-time data contradicts the current loop hypothesis

pros.claim: explains collapse despite each actor behaving rationally
pros.example: overfishing a shared stock to depletion

pros.claim: points leverage to the shared resource and feedback to actors
pros.example: quota or feedback making the commons visible

cons.claim: the shared-limit loop is invisible to individual actors
cons.example: each fisher ignores the aggregate stock

cons.claim: requires modeling multiple actors, raising complexity
cons.example: many symmetric reinforcing loops

failure_modes: modeling one actor and missing the aggregate
no feedback from the resource to actors
leverage placed on exhortation not structure
acceptance_tests: multiple per-actor reinforcing loops and a shared resource limit are identified
resource feedback to actors is examined
leverage addresses the shared structure
revisit_triggers: a new actor enters the commons

nodes.definition: Match a fix that relieves a symptom now but triggers a delayed reinforcing consequence that worsens it later to the fixes-that-fail archetype.

included: pattern matching to the named archetype

contradictors: analyst who treats each problem as unique with no recurring structure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new behavior-over-time data contradicts the current loop hypothesis

pros.claim: the delay explains why the fix looks good before it backfires
pros.example: cutting maintenance saves cost then breaks equipment

pros.claim: foregrounds the unintended-consequence loop
pros.example: debt papering over a shortfall, compounding later

cons.claim: the delayed consequence loop is the hardest to see in advance
cons.example: the backfire arrives after the credit is taken

cons.claim: easily confused with shifting-the-burden
cons.example: fix-that-fails vs symptomatic dependence

failure_modes: claiming success before the delayed loop acts
ignoring the unintended-consequence loop
attributing the backfire to a new external cause
acceptance_tests: a fix loop and a delayed reinforcing consequence loop are identified
the delay between fix and backfire is estimated
the unintended consequence is traced to the fix

nodes.definition: Match resource allocation that favors an already-winning option, starving alternatives, to the success-to-the-successful archetype with two coupled reinforcing loops sharing a constraint.

included: pattern matching to the named archetype

contradictors: analyst who treats each problem as unique with no recurring structure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new behavior-over-time data contradicts the current loop hypothesis

pros.claim: explains lock-in and winner-take-all from small initial differences
pros.example: one product gets all the marketing, the other withers

pros.claim: leverage lies in the allocation rule, not the contestants
pros.example: decoupling funding from prior success

cons.claim: the shared-allocation link is easy to overlook
cons.example: not seeing that both draw on one budget

cons.claim: path dependence makes it look like merit
cons.example: attributing lock-in to quality alone

failure_modes: explaining lock-in by intrinsic merit
missing the shared-resource coupling
allocation rule treated as fixed
acceptance_tests: two reinforcing loops coupled through a shared resource are identified
the allocation rule linking them is named
leverage targets the allocation rule

nodes.definition: Locate where a small structural change yields a large lasting behavior change, ranking candidate interventions on a leverage hierarchy (parameters low; goals, rules, paradigms high).
contradictors: analyst who tunes parameters and ignores structure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a higher-order leverage point (rules, goals, paradigm) is found that outranks the current one

pros.claim: high leverage (rules, goals, paradigms) beats parameter-tweaking for lasting change
pros.example: changing the goal, not the gain

pros.claim: targeting the dominant or constraining loop concentrates effort
pros.example: relaxing the binding limit in limits-to-growth

cons.claim: high-leverage points are often counterintuitive and pushed in the wrong direction
cons.example: subsidizing the symptom and worsening it

cons.claim: leverage is irreversible-ish: structural change is hard to undo
cons.example: re-architecting an incentive system

failure_modes: intervening on a low-leverage parameter
pushing a leverage point in the wrong direction
ignoring the dominant loop
acceptance_tests: candidate interventions ranked on a leverage hierarchy
each intervention names the loop it changes
direction of push is justified against behavior
revisit_triggers: a higher-order leverage point is found
an intervention has the opposite effect

nodes.definition: Identify thresholds where a small change pushes the system across a nonlinearity into a qualitatively different, often hard-to-reverse regime, and bound their location.
contradictors: analyst who assumes linear, gradual response

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a threshold estimate is revised or a new nonlinearity is found

pros.claim: naming a tipping point flags where gradual policy suddenly fails
pros.example: an ecosystem crossing into collapse

pros.claim: early-warning indicators give a chance to act before the threshold
pros.example: rising variance signaling a nearing shift

cons.claim: threshold location is highly uncertain without data
cons.example: not knowing how close the system is

cons.claim: crossing can be irreversible (hysteresis)
cons.example: a lake that will not de-eutrophy easily

failure_modes: assuming linear response near a threshold
threshold located with false precision
ignoring hysteresis after crossing
acceptance_tests: each tipping point is bounded, not given false precision
hysteresis/irreversibility is assessed
an early-warning indicator is proposed

nodes.definition: Characterize pure reinforcing-loop behavior as exponential growth (or decay), estimate its doubling/halving time, and flag that unchecked growth must eventually meet a limit.
contradictors: analyst who extrapolates exponentials linearly

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the doubling time or driving reinforcing loop is re-estimated

pros.claim: recognizing exponential behavior prevents linear underestimation
pros.example: compounding interest or viral spread

pros.claim: doubling time makes the speed of a reinforcing loop concrete
pros.example: a quantity that doubles every quarter

cons.claim: no real system grows exponentially forever; a limit always binds
cons.example: forecasting unbounded growth

cons.claim: early exponential and linear data look alike
cons.example: mistaking early growth for slow linear

failure_modes: extrapolating an exponential linearly
ignoring the inevitable limit
confusing growth with a one-time jump
acceptance_tests: growth is tied to an identified reinforcing loop
a doubling/halving time is estimated
a downstream limit is flagged for search

nodes.definition: Diagnose overshoot-and-collapse: a reinforcing loop drives a stock past a limit that itself erodes, with delays preventing timely correction, leading to collapse rather than a smooth plateau.
contradictors: analyst who expects S-shaped approach to every limit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the delay or erodible-limit assumption behind the collapse is revised

pros.claim: distinguishes catastrophic collapse from a safe plateau
pros.example: a population overshooting and crashing its food base

pros.claim: foregrounds the erodible carrying capacity as the danger
pros.example: resource use degrading the very limit

cons.claim: collapse depends on delays and erosion that are hard to quantify
cons.example: not knowing how fast the limit erodes

cons.claim: often irreversible once collapse begins
cons.example: a degraded resource that cannot recover

failure_modes: assuming S-shaped approach when the limit erodes
ignoring the delay that defeats correction
mistaking overshoot for normal growth
acceptance_tests: a reinforcing driver and an erodible limit are both identified
delays that prevent timely correction are named
irreversibility of collapse is assessed

nodes.definition: Trace how an intervention propagates through delayed and distant feedback to produce side effects, policy resistance, or worse-before-better dynamics, before the intervention is committed.
contradictors: analyst who evaluates an intervention only by its intended direct effect

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new delayed side-effect loop is discovered for an intervention

pros.claim: surfaces policy resistance and side effects before commitment

pros.claim: the delay lens explains worse-before-better and backfire
pros.example: tightening then loosening as the system adapts

cons.claim: side-effect chains are long and easy to truncate too early
cons.example: stopping the trace before the harmful loop

cons.claim: hard to bound without simulation
cons.example: every intervention has indefinitely many ripples

failure_modes: evaluating only the intended direct effect
truncating the side-effect trace too early
ignoring policy resistance
acceptance_tests: each intervention is traced through at least one delayed feedback path

nodes.definition: Test whether the loop/structure hypothesis reproduces the reference mode and known behavior patterns (growth, goal-seeking, oscillation, S-shape, overshoot) qualitatively before any claim is locked.

nodes.definition: Surface and reconcile stakeholders' mental models of cause and effect into explicit signed links and loops, exposing hidden assumptions and disagreements about structure.

edges.why_related: the CLD is usually elaborated into an SFD; loops should match
edges.risk_of_conflict: an SFD whose loops differ from the CLD signals an error
edges.resolution_rule: reconcile SFD loops with the CLD

edges.why_related: the archetype is matched from polarity-labeled R and B loops
edges.risk_of_conflict: matching without polarity is pattern-forcing
edges.resolution_rule: classify polarity before matching the archetype

edges.why_related: shifting-the-burden requires identified symptomatic and fundamental loops
edges.risk_of_conflict: forcing the pattern without loops misleads
edges.resolution_rule: identify loops before matching

edges.why_related: the commons pattern needs per-actor reinforcing loops and a shared limit
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing the shared loop breaks the match
edges.resolution_rule: classify loops before matching

edges.why_related: fixes-that-fail depends on a delay before the reinforcing consequence acts
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring the delay loses the archetype
edges.resolution_rule: identify the delay before matching fixes-that-fail

edges.why_related: the archetype needs two coupled reinforcing loops sharing a resource
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing the coupling breaks the match
edges.resolution_rule: classify the loops before matching

edges.why_related: limits-to-growth is realized as a dominance shift from R to B
edges.risk_of_conflict: an archetype with no shift is static
edges.example: the archetype shows the R->B shift
edges.resolution_rule: tie the archetype to the dominance shift

edges.why_related: leverage targets the dominant or constraining loop, so dominance must be known
edges.risk_of_conflict: leverage without dominance is parameter-tweaking
edges.resolution_rule: find dominance before choosing leverage

edges.why_related: knowing where dominance shifts reveals where a structural change has most effect
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring shifts misplaces leverage
edges.resolution_rule: use the shift timeline to place leverage

edges.why_related: abrupt dominance shifts at nonlinearities are tipping points
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing the nonlinearity hides the tipping point
edges.example: tipping points bound the abrupt shift
edges.resolution_rule: analyze shifts to bound tipping points

edges.why_related: a pure reinforcing loop produces exponential growth
edges.risk_of_conflict: mislabeling polarity misreads growth
edges.example: growth tied to an R loop
edges.resolution_rule: confirm reinforcing polarity before claiming exponential growth

edges.why_related: unbounded exponential growth prompts a search for the limit that will bind
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring the limit forecasts impossible growth
edges.resolution_rule: after characterizing growth, search for its limit

edges.why_related: delays that defeat correction are the mechanism of overshoot-and-collapse
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring delays predicts a safe plateau
edges.resolution_rule: attribute collapse to the correction-defeating delay

edges.why_related: growth past an erodible limit with delays yields collapse not plateau
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating it as plateau understates risk
edges.resolution_rule: check whether growth overshoots an erodible limit

edges.why_related: candidate leverage interventions must be checked for delayed side effects
edges.risk_of_conflict: unchecked leverage causes policy resistance
edges.resolution_rule: trace consequences before committing leverage

edges.why_related: delayed feedback is what turns an intervention into a surprise
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring delays hides worse-before-better
edges.resolution_rule: trace delayed feedback for each intervention

edges.why_related: validation tests whether the dominant-loop hypothesis reproduces behavior
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unvalidated dominance claim is unsafe
edges.resolution_rule: validate the dominance hypothesis against behavior

edges.why_related: the diagrammed structure is what gets behavior-tested
edges.risk_of_conflict: testing an undiagrammed structure is ad hoc
edges.resolution_rule: diagram the structure before behavior validation

edges.why_related: failed behavior validation triggers revisiting the dominance hypothesis
edges.risk_of_conflict: without this loop wrong dominance persists
edges.example: revisit dominance on validation failure; stop when behavior reproduced
edges.resolution_rule: on failed validation, revisit dominance; stop when the reference mode is reproduced

edges.why_related: elicited mental models inform what the purpose and boundary should include
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping elicitation narrows the boundary wrongly
edges.resolution_rule: elicit mental models to inform the boundary

edges.why_related: stakeholder mental models surface candidate loops to trace
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring stakeholders misses real loops
edges.resolution_rule: use elicited models as loop candidates

edges.why_related: validation gaps trigger re-eliciting stakeholder models for missing structure
edges.risk_of_conflict: without it, missing loops stay missing
edges.example: re-elicit on unexplained behavior; stop when behavior is reproduced
edges.resolution_rule: on validation gaps, re-elicit; stop once the structure reproduces behavior

edges.why_related: CLD readability for stakeholders trades off against SFD rigor on accumulation
edges.risk_of_conflict: optimizing one degrades the other
edges.example: pick CLD for communication, SFD for accumulation rigor; keep loops consistent
edges.resolution_rule: use a CLD to communicate and an SFD where accumulation matters, reconciling loops

edges.why_related: high-leverage structural change maximizes impact but maximizes side-effect risk
edges.risk_of_conflict: chasing impact can trigger policy resistance
edges.example: prefer leverage whose side effects are bounded and reversible
edges.resolution_rule: when a high-leverage point has unbounded side effects, choose a lower-leverage, safer one

edges.why_related: extrapolating growth conflicts with anticipating the dominance shift that ends it
edges.risk_of_conflict: pure extrapolation ignores the coming shift
edges.resolution_rule: let the expected dominance shift override exponential extrapolation

edges.why_related: acting near a tipping point gives high leverage but high irreversibility
edges.risk_of_conflict: strong action near a threshold can cause an irreversible regime shift
edges.example: require human review before leverage that risks crossing a tipping point
edges.resolution_rule: escalate to human review when leverage could push the system across a tipping point

conflict_axes.trigger: a reinforcing loop is pushed for growth while a balancing loop seeks stability
resolution_order: identify the decision's time horizon
determine whether growth or stability serves it
name which loop must dominate and why
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the loop whose behavior serves the stated purpose over the time horizon dominates; the other is bounded
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: growth is pursued with no limit and no stabilizing loop
conflict_axes.example: promoting growth with no plan for the limit that will bind

conflict_axes.trigger: a CLD is clear to stakeholders but a SFD is needed to be faithful to accumulation
resolution_order: state whether the artifact is for communication or analysis
use a CLD to communicate, an SFD where accumulation matters
reconcile loops across both
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: accumulation-faithful SFD dominates when conclusions depend on stocks; CLD dominates for communication
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a CLD-only model is used to draw stock-dependent conclusions
conflict_axes.example: claiming equilibrium from a CLD that hides an accumulating stock

conflict_axes.trigger: the highest-leverage intervention also carries the largest side-effect risk
resolution_order: bound the side effects of each candidate
prefer high-leverage interventions whose side effects are bounded and reversible
escalate irreversible high-leverage moves
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: bounded, reversible leverage dominates; unbounded high-leverage moves require human review
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a high-leverage change has unbounded or irreversible side effects
conflict_axes.example: a structural change that maximizes impact and triggers severe policy resistance

conflict_axes.trigger: early exponential data invites extrapolation while a dominance shift is imminent
resolution_order: check whether a limit or balancing loop is approaching
if a shift is expected, prefer anticipation over extrapolation
document the expected shift trigger
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: anticipated dominance shift dominates naive extrapolation when a limit is plausible
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: extrapolation is used past the point a limit plausibly binds
conflict_axes.example: forecasting continued exponential growth into a saturating market

conflict_axes.trigger: a simple bounded model may omit a loop that actually drives behavior
resolution_order: test whether the current loop set reproduces the reference mode
if not, widen the boundary minimally to admit the missing loop
keep the model as simple as the purpose allows
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: completeness wins only for loops needed to reproduce the reference mode; otherwise simplicity dominates
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the reference mode cannot be reproduced by the current loops
conflict_axes.example: excluding word-of-mouth and then failing to reproduce adoption

conflict_axes.trigger: a symptomatic quick fix competes with the fundamental solution for resources
resolution_order: identify the symptomatic and fundamental loops
check for an erosion/addiction side-effect
direct leverage to the fundamental solution
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the fundamental solution dominates; quick fixes are bounded to avoid eroding it
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: reliance on the quick fix is eroding the fundamental capability
conflict_axes.example: more painkillers while the cure program is defunded

conflict_axes.trigger: each actor optimizing locally degrades the shared system outcome
resolution_order: model the aggregate effect of local actions
validate against the system-level behavior
add resource feedback to actors
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: system-level validated behavior dominates local rationality when they conflict
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: local-optimal actions drive the shared resource toward collapse
conflict_axes.example: each unit maximizing throughput and collapsing a shared resource

conflict_axes.trigger: a recommendation is wanted before the structure is behavior-validated
resolution_order: block irreversible recommendations until validation passes
allow reversible, low-risk actions in draft
record any speed-over-validation override
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: behavior validation dominates for any high-risk or irreversible recommendation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an irreversible intervention is recommended before validation
conflict_axes.example: issuing a leverage recommendation from an unvalidated CLD

edge_cases.trigger: an open causal chain is treated as a closed feedback loop
edge_cases.example: labeling a one-way price->sales chain as a balancing loop
edge_cases.detection_method: check that each claimed loop returns to its starting variable
resolution: reject loops that do not close
re-trace the chain to its origin or drop it

edge_cases.trigger: a link is signed by whether the outcome is desirable, not by mechanism
edge_cases.detection_method: audit each link sign against the all-else-equal increase/decrease test
resolution: downgrade to associational and re-sign by mechanism
split non-monotonic links

edge_cases.trigger: loop dominance is asserted from a static diagram with no behavior evidence
edge_cases.example: claiming the reinforcing loop dominates from arrow count alone
edge_cases.detection_method: require the dominant loop to reproduce the observed behavior pattern
resolution: attach behavior-over-time evidence
downgrade dominance claim to a hypothesis

edge_cases.trigger: a delay is omitted so oscillation/overshoot is invisible
edge_cases.failure_mode: model predicts smooth response where reality oscillates
edge_cases.example: a workforce model with instant hiring that cannot oscillate
edge_cases.detection_method: check every balancing loop for an internal delay
resolution: add the missing delay
re-test for oscillation against the reference mode

edge_cases.trigger: exponential growth is extrapolated past a limit that will bind
edge_cases.example: forecasting endless growth into a saturating market
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether a limit or balancing loop is approaching the trajectory
resolution: search for the binding limit
replace extrapolation with a dominance-shift scenario

edge_cases.trigger: a reinforcing loop is modeled with no limit ever binding
edge_cases.example: an adoption model with no saturation
edge_cases.detection_method: require a limit-search flag for every dominant reinforcing loop
resolution: add the constraining balancing loop
bound the growth horizon

edge_cases.trigger: a high-leverage intervention is recommended without tracing side effects
edge_cases.example: a subsidy recommended that the system later neutralizes
edge_cases.detection_method: require each intervention to be traced through at least one delayed feedback path
resolution: trace delayed side effects
prefer a bounded, reversible alternative

edge_cases.trigger: stock-dependent conclusions are drawn from a CLD that hides accumulation
edge_cases.example: a CLD that looks balanced while a stock keeps accumulating
edge_cases.detection_method: cross-check CLD conclusions against an SFD where stocks matter
resolution: build the SFD for the accumulating part
reconcile loops across CLD and SFD

edge_cases.trigger: an archetype is force-fit without confirming its loop structure
edge_cases.failure_mode: wrong leverage from a mismatched archetype
edge_cases.example: labeling a constraint problem as shifting-the-burden
edge_cases.detection_method: require the archetype's named loops to be present and labeled
resolution: confirm the loop structure
choose the archetype whose loops actually match

edge_cases.trigger: a tipping-point threshold is stated with false precision
edge_cases.example: claiming a regime shift at an exact value with no data
edge_cases.detection_method: require thresholds to be bounded ranges with uncertainty
resolution: replace point estimate with a bounded range
add an early-warning indicator

edge_cases.trigger: a computed score or evidence label is inconsistent with its inputs
edge_cases.example: a final_importance not matching the node formula, or an observed label with no data
edge_cases.detection_method: re-run the formula script and the evidence-label check
resolution: recompute all derived fields from the schema formulas
reset illegal labels to heuristic

workflow.objective: fix the purpose, reference mode, boundary, and surface stakeholder mental models
entry_criteria: a symptom and a decision are stated
acceptance_tests: a reference mode graph exists
each key variable is endogenous/exogenous with reason
workflow.do_first_because: the boundary and reference mode are the highest-coupling foundation every later choice inherits

workflow.objective: classify stocks and flows and locate delays
acceptance_tests: each stock has a named flow
units of flows match stocks per time
workflow.do_first_because: accumulation and delays underlie every loop and must be stable before loops are traced

workflow.objective: enumerate closed loops and sign every link
acceptance_tests: each loop closes to its origin
each link sign passes the all-else-equal test
workflow.do_first_because: loops and signs are the atomic inputs to polarity, dominance, and archetypes

workflow.objective: classify each loop as reinforcing or balancing by parity of negative links
acceptance_tests: polarity equals parity of negative links for every loop
workflow.do_first_because: polarity gates dominance, archetypes, growth, and diagramming

workflow.objective: render the structure as a CLD and, where accumulation matters, an SFD
acceptance_tests: every loop is R/B labeled on the CLD
every flow conserves units in the SFD
workflow.do_first_because: the diagram is the testable artifact for validation and the bridge to simulation

workflow.objective: assign the dominant loop per phase and locate dominance shifts
acceptance_tests: the dominant loop reproduces the observed pattern
each inflection has a named shift
workflow.do_first_because: dominance focuses where archetypes and leverage should act

workflow.objective: match the loop structure to recurring system archetypes
acceptance_tests: each match cites the archetype's named loops present in the model
workflow.do_first_because: archetypes turn structure into recognized leverage patterns

workflow.objective: characterize growth, bound tipping points, and diagnose overshoot-and-collapse
acceptance_tests: growth is tied to an R loop with a limit-search flag
thresholds are bounded ranges
collapse irreversibility is assessed
workflow.do_first_because: nonlinear and irreversible risks must be flagged before any intervention is chosen

workflow.objective: rank leverage points and trace each intervention's unintended consequences
acceptance_tests: each intervention names the loop it changes
each is traced through a delayed feedback path
workflow.do_first_because: leverage is the highest-value output and must be guarded against backfire and irreversibility

workflow.objective: test that the structure reproduces the reference mode and known behavior modes
acceptance_tests: the structure reproduces the reference mode qualitatively
each known behavior mode is tested
workflow.do_first_because: no claim is locked until the structure demonstrably reproduces the target behavior

priority_rationale.notes: root scope every later choice inherits
surfaces loops before structure is fixed
accumulation structure underlies loops and delays
loops are the unit later steps classify
signed links feed polarity and the CLD
shifts explain real behavior and nonlinearity

dominance_rules.trigger: a recommendation is wanted before high-risk structure is validated
dominance_rules.rule: high-risk or irreversible conclusions wait for behavior validation
dominance_rules.required_action: block the conclusion until validation passes
dominance_rules.example: refusing a leverage recommendation from an unvalidated model

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is ready before its prerequisite
dominance_rules.example: not classifying polarity before signing links

dominance_rules.rule: evidence-label correctness dominates apparent numeric precision
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade to heuristic and widen uncertainty
dominance_rules.example: not stating a tipping point to three decimals without data

dominance_rules.trigger: a structure is about to be locked before validation
dominance_rules.rule: behavior validation must pass before any hard lock
dominance_rules.example: not hard-locking a CLD that fails to reproduce the reference mode

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-leverage decision is reached
dominance_rules.rule: human review overrides automation for irreversible or tipping-point-crossing actions
dominance_rules.example: escalating leverage that could cross a tipping point

dominance_rules.rule: schema stability dominates raw count of nodes/edges
dominance_rules.required_action: stop adding and repair structure first
dominance_rules.example: not padding with near-duplicate archetype nodes

dominance_rules.trigger: output formatting conflicts with strict JSON
dominance_rules.rule: strict JSON validity dominates prose niceties
dominance_rules.example: no markdown or comments in the KB file

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim exceeds what the source supports
dominance_rules.example: labeling heuristic loop weights as observed is forbidden

dominance_rules.trigger: a locally optimal step would force later rework
dominance_rules.example: not drawing the SFD before stocks/flows are typed

dominance_rules.trigger: a score uses a hidden or undefined input
dominance_rules.rule: explicit formula inputs dominate hidden assumptions
dominance_rules.example: every score recomputed by the formula script from declared inputs

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the purpose and boundary before typing structure
anti_rework_rules.rationale: structure built outside a stable boundary is reworked when the boundary shifts
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: stocks typed before the boundary is set
anti_rework_rules.example: typing economy-wide variables for a single-product model

anti_rework_rules.rule: elicit stakeholder mental models before locking structure
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a model built without stakeholders misses real loops and is reworked
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: loops finalized with no stakeholder input
anti_rework_rules.example: missing an operator-known feedback the manual omits

anti_rework_rules.rule: type stocks and flows before tracing loops
anti_rework_rules.rationale: loops ignoring accumulation are unphysical and must be redrawn

anti_rework_rules.rule: sign every link before classifying loop polarity
anti_rework_rules.rationale: polarity without signed links is guesswork and gets reversed later
dominance over unlabeled loops is unfounded
anti_rework_rules.example: ranking loops with no R/B labels

anti_rework_rules.rationale: without delays the model cannot show the oscillation it must explain
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: overshoot diagnosed with no delays present
anti_rework_rules.example: a balancing loop with no internal delay that cannot oscillate

anti_rework_rules.rule: find the dominant loop before choosing leverage
anti_rework_rules.rationale: leverage without dominance degenerates into parameter-tweaking
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: leverage chosen with no dominance analysis
anti_rework_rules.example: tuning a gain instead of changing the binding rule

anti_rework_rules.rule: trace unintended consequences before committing leverage
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an untraced intervention causes policy resistance and rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a recommendation with no side-effect trace
anti_rework_rules.example: a subsidy the system later neutralizes

anti_rework_rules.rule: behavior-validate the structure before any hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking an unvalidated structure forces a full re-do when behavior fails
anti_rework_rules.example: locking a model that cannot reproduce the reference mode

anti_rework_rules.rule: recompute all derived fields after any metric change
anti_rework_rules.rationale: stale derived scores fail formula consistency and trigger rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a final_importance inconsistent with its inputs
anti_rework_rules.example: editing a base metric without re-running the formula script

iteration_protocol.trigger: the validator or a behavior test reports a failure
iteration_protocol.detection: compare validation_report checks and behavior coverage to thresholds
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and downstream coupling
action: score defects by risk and coupling
acceptance_tests: high-risk defects ranked first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only low-risk warnings remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fix would touch a high-coupling or locked node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents of the node to be changed
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the change are listed
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no high-coupling node changes remain unanalyzed

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is ready to fix
iteration_protocol.detection: map the defect class to its repair subsystem
acceptance_tests: each defect routed to a single owner

iteration_protocol.trigger: a base metric or interval changed
iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the formula script over the KB
acceptance_tests: all derived fields match the formulas within tolerance

iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator and behavior tests
acceptance_tests: no new failures introduced
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: validator passes and behavior is reproduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence about a loop or threshold arrives
iteration_protocol.detection: compare new evidence to prior importance
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed as PI*EC with no observed data
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior change below the revisit delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: an irreversible or tipping-point-crossing decision is reached
acceptance_tests: every high-risk/irreversible item escalated
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: all such items have a human decision record
